name: box_twelve_triangles
why: A BOX MAKES TWELVE TRIANGLES, always: six planar faces, two triangles each. It is not a plausible number, it is an exact number -- and it is what makes this case a measurement instead of a «the file is there and weighs something».
_why_the_bytes: a binary STL is 80 bytes of header, 4 with the number of triangles, then 50 per triangle: 84 + 50*12 = 684. The file must weigh EXACTLY that. If the count does not add up, the file opens all the same and is not the part -- and this is the only place in the whole chain where it can be seen.

expect._why_twelve: six planar faces, two triangles each

expect._why_684: 84 + 50*12: the header plus the twelve triangles

expect.why: it is the default, and an ASCII one would weigh ten times as much
the file does NOT carry them with it and the slicer assumes millimetres: if this line were not there, the only possible answer would be «dunno, just try»

includes: after the header of the binary file
expect.why: the triangles are counted by RE-READING THE FILE, not by asking whoever wrote it

includes: as geometry it can be exported
expect.why: the check REALLY ran before writing, and its sentence travels with the answer. That the field «exported_anyway» is not here is proved by the case `two_bodies_exported_by_force`, where it is
